definition: Divulge means to make something secret known to others.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word divulge. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know divulge should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Jury members are warned never to divulge what was said in the deliberation room, even years after the verdict.
Hint is milder than divulge — a hint lets one corner of the secret show and makes the listener do the rest of the work.
Trumpet goes further than divulge: to divulge is to pass the secret to someone, while to trumpet it is to blast it to everyone in earshot.

To reveal is simply to make something visible or known, and no secret is required — a curtain can reveal a stage. To divulge is narrower: a genuine secret crosses a boundary, handed deliberately to someone outside the circle. Reveal is neutral; divulge accuses.

To let slip is to release a secret by accident — a name dropped mid-story before the speaker can catch it. Divulging is the deliberate act: the teller chooses to hand the secret over. Both cross the line, but only divulge does it on purpose.

New performers at the Wonderpark sign what veterans call 'the quiet page' before they are ever fitted for a costume.
The rules are strict: never divulge who wears which character, not to friends, not to family, not even to other employees outside the costume department.
The logic is commercial, but the staff treat it as something closer to an ethic.
